didrun_findings.scope: concurrent session append and chain integrity
didrun_findings.effect: Concurrent writers can fork the ledger, invalidate claim addressing, and leave the session unusable as evidence.
didrun_findings.summary: Tail read and append are not protected by an interprocess lock.

didrun_findings.scope: wrapped command output and operator liveness
didrun_findings.effect: Recorded failures require direct immutable-blob inspection, while long commands provide no bounded progress signal.
didrun_findings.summary: The CLI retains wrapped output but does not expose it or stream bounded progress.

didrun_findings.scope: entropy scanning and redacted evidence export
didrun_findings.effect: Ordinary digests and fixtures cause aggregate secret warnings without enough locality for precise classification.
didrun_findings.summary: High-entropy findings have high false-positive pressure and expose only an aggregate count.

didrun_findings.scope: claim addressing and strict verification on forked ledgers
didrun_findings.effect: Duplicate stored indices can misbind claims, and strict verification can fail open unless chain integrity is checked separately.
didrun_findings.summary: Claims use unstable physical offsets and sealing does not first reject a forked session chain.

didrun_findings.scope: Git-note publication and local seal state
didrun_findings.effect: A denied note write can return success and advance the local seal watermark despite absent commit-bound evidence.
didrun_findings.summary: Seal publication is not atomic or fail-closed across local state and the Git note.

didrun_findings.scope: portable strict verification of archived ledgers
didrun_findings.effect: A sealed commit becomes UNKNOWN when its matching ignored ledger moves, even though its Git note remains present.
didrun_findings.summary: Strict verification cannot select an archived witness ledger and the Git note is not self-sufficient.
